III. Calculating HAP for Voucher Tenancy
The “space rent” is subject to rent reasonableness determination.
The amount of the monthly housing assistance payment for a family will
equal the lesser of:
• The payment standard minus the TTP; or
• The total rent of the manufactured home space as defined above
minus the TTP .
If the amount of the monthly assistance payment for a family exceeds the
monthly rent for the manufactured home space (including monthly
management and maintenance charges), the PHA will pay the remainder to
the family.
The family is responsible to promptly notify the NHA of any changes in their
monthly loan payment amount and advise the NHA if they have stopped
making their monthly payments for any reason.

PROJECT-BASED ASSISTANCE
I. Overall Approach
The NHA may attach up to 30% of baseline units to existing units, units for
rehabilitation or new construction under the Project -Based Voucher (PBV)
Program. Project -basing may be considered an option for securing long -term
affordability for existing low -income units or “at risk” pro jects, a strategy for
improving lease-up in a tight rental environment, and/or a method of financing the
construction of affordable rental housing.
II. Project Selection Policy
The projected number of units to be assisted under project-based Section 8 will be
determined annually and described in the Public Housing Agency (PHA) Annual
Plan. The project selection criteria, including eligible unit types, is described in this
section of the Administrative Plan. The NHA may attach assistance to the greater
of 25% of the units in a project or 25 units, up to 40% of the units in a project
located in a census tract with a poverty rate of 20% or less, or up to 100% of the
units if the project is designated for elderly tenants or is for households eligible for
supportive services. PBV will not be provided to group homes, cooperative
housing, shared housing, transitional housing, or nursing homes.
The availability of PBV funding will be announced periodically through a
competitive process. The deadline for submission of proposals will be set at the
time of the announcement and will vary depending upon the type of project
proposals being solicited, b ut generally will be 30 -60 days. Proposal evaluation
criteria will include capacity and experience of developer, financial viability of the
project, design/rehabilitation scope of work, project amenities, location, and
neighborhood amenities. Points will b e awarded based on how well the project
meets the evaluation criteria. Specific details on proposal submission and rating
procedures will be posted on the City’s website.
Proposed sites will be reviewed in accordance with 24 CFR 983.57(b)(1) and the
site selection standards described in the PHA Plan. Sites located in census tracts
with low poverty rates or in/adjacent to economic opportunity areas will receive
more points during the evaluation phase. For existing and rehabilitated housing
projects, sites with access to public transportation, near major thoroughfares and
near jobs and services will receive greater consideration. For new construction
projects, sites will be ev aluated based upon 24 CFR 983.57 ( e). Greater
consideration will be given to proposals that accomplish deconcentration goals and
are in census block groups that currently lack assisted projects.

The NHA will advertise in a local newspaper with general circulation and post

The project selection date is the date of t NHA Commission approval. The results

III. Contract Length and Extensions
The length of the Contract will vary from five to twenty years depending upon the
needs of the project as determined by the Commission. Contract extensions and
the length of extensions will be subject to Commission approval.
IV. Eligibility and Tenant Selection
The NHA will also be responsible for managing the waiting list and tenant selection
for each project. Placement and selection on the list will differ between projects
based upon the population that the project is targeting (e.g. elderly, veterans, or
homeless). The NHA will use the regular Section 8 waiting list to make selections
for project-based units before establishing a separate waiting list. The Section 8
waiting list gives preference to existing tenants of a building selected for project -
based assistance. The tenants must be eligible for Section 8 to receive the subsidy.
If a separate waiting list is established, the list may be opened or closed
independent of the regular Section 8 waiting list.
The NHA will be responsible for reviewing each tenant’s eligibility before referring
the applicant to the project for further screening. If the unit is for a household
eligible for supportive services, eligibility will be verified by a service provider or
other knowledgeable professional. During the eligibility interview an eligible
applicant will be given information about the project. If the applicant is interested
in applying for the project, referral to the project owner or manager will be made.
The NHA will attempt to refer 2 -3 eligible applicants for each vacant unit. If an
applicant does not want the project-based unit or is not selected by the owner, the
applicant will be returned to the tenant -based voucher waiting list only if the
applicant had als o applied for a tenant -based voucher. If the applicant wants a
project-based unit, but the unit is not available, the applicant may choose to be
placed back on the waiting list until a unit becomes available.
At the time of the eligibility interview, if the applicant has a choice of tenant-based
or project-based assistance and no tenant-based vouchers are available, then the
applicant will be returned to the waiting list until a voucher becomes available. If

the applicant was given priority due to the project’s specific selection criteria (i.e.
elderly or disabled) and the applicant does not want the project-based assistance,
their application will also be returned to the waiting list. Applicants who reject tw o
unit offers will be removed from the PBV waiting list or returned to the tenant-based
waiting list.
Eligibility for a project-based voucher is the same as the Section 8 eligibility criteria
described earlier in this plan.
V. Overcrowded, Under-Occupied Units
Should the household size increase or decrease requiring a change of unit, the
household will be offered either the first available unit appropriate for their
household size or a tenant based voucher, if available. The tenant does not have
to accept a tenant-based voucher if they want to wait for the next suitable unit. If
the tenant elects to wait for the next unit but refuses the unit offered, the household
will be required to accept a tenant-based voucher when one is available and move
before the expiration of the voucher.
VI. Contract Rent and Rent Adjustments
The gross rent (rent plus allowance for tenant -paid utilities) requested for the
assisted units must be rent reasonable and cannot exceed the NHA’s payment
standard or other limit set by HUD.
Contract rent and rent adjustments will be negotiated with the project’s owner prior
to Contract execution and annually thereafter. The Contract and amendments will
detail the approved rent.
Tenant recertifications will be effective on the anniversary date of the Contract. The
latest Utility Allowance Schedule will be applied to the tenant’s rent calculation
during the annual recertification.
VII. Moving and Portability
A tenant, who has received project -based assistance for at least one year, may
request a tenant-based voucher in order to move. That tenant may elect to move
to another unit in Norwalk or transfer under portability. If a tenant -based voucher
is not available at the time of the move, the tenant will receive the next available
voucher. The project-based unit vacated by the household will remain subsidized.
The NHA will refer eligible households from the waiting list to fill the slot.
VIII. Vacancies
At the NHA’s discretion, the contract with the owner may provide for up to two
